title: Towards Redundancy-Free Recommendation Model Training via Reusable-aware Near-Memory Processing
problem: The memory-intensive embedding layer in recommendation models is a critical performance bottleneck. Static cache solutions fail in training scenarios where embedding vectors are updated frequently, making real-time data reuse identification necessary.
motivation: Improving embedding layer efficiency during training directly impacts the scalability and energy efficiency of recommendation system deployment.
method: ReFree performs real-time identification of reusable data for both embedding forward and backward stages. It employs a lightweight near-memory processing architecture that exploits data locality to eliminate redundant memory operations and memory traffic throughout the entire embedding training pipeline.
key_novelty: Real-time reusable data identification for dynamic embedding training combined with lightweight NMP architecture to achieve redundancy-free acceleration.
contributions: Identifies the failure of static caching for dynamic embedding training with frequent vector updates
Proposes real-time reusable data identification mechanism for forward and backward passes
Designs lightweight near-memory processing architecture for redundancy elimination
Achieves 10.9× speedup and 5.3× energy reduction versus state-of-the-art embedding optimization
baselines: Prior embedding optimization works with static caching
limitations: Specific limitations and applicability boundaries not discussed in abstract
primary_theme: Redundancy-free near-memory acceleration for embedding training
